To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structures of two novel compounds Sr(3)(Be)(2)(B)(5)O(11)(OH) (Sr-3-B2) and Ba(2)(Be)(2)B(2)O(11) (Ba-3-B2), have been determined by single crystal X-ray diffraction.
the structures consist of a 3D network of BO(3), BeO(4), and MO(9) (M = Sr or Ba) polyhedral units.

the compounds Sr(3)(Be(2)BO(3))(2)(OH) and Ba(4)(Be(2)(BO(3))(3)(OH) are the first acentric compounds of the general formula (M(3)BeB(5)BO(12)(OH)), which crystallize in space group R3 m and are isostructural with each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of novel compounds with interesting properties, and the present study is an attempt to understand the role of building blocks in imparting the noncentrosymmetry in these compounds.
the design of a new class of materials with acentric structures based on acentric building units such as BO(3), BO(4), and BeO(3).
acentricity in the solid state.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these compounds are the first examples of the acentric berylloborate family.
the presence of the polar BO(3) group is the driving force for the acentricity in these compounds.
the presence of the acentric building block [Be(2)(BO)(4)](6+) is a prerequisite for noncentrosymmetricity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the acentric building units of [BO(4)O](5-) and [BO(3)O](3-) are able to form noncentrosymmetric structures with the aid of the [BeO(3)](4-) building unit, which is also acentric in character.
acentric borate building blocks can be used as a tool to synthesize acentric materials.
the presence of acentric building units in a structure is not sufficient to impart acentricity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of acentric building units in the construction of acentric structures is not limited to only those with a single connectivity, such as [BO3](3-) and [BO4](5-) units.
the combination of acentric building units and the presence of a 3-fold axis can be a viable route to the synthesis of new noncentrosymmetric compounds.
the combination of acentric building units with acentricity imparting networks can lead to the formation of new noncentrosymmetric compounds.
